entities.name: Apostle Paul (Saul of Tarsus)
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: The most influential figure in the spread of early Christianity (c. 5–64 CE). Originally a Pharisee persecuting Christians, his dramatic conversion on the Damascus road led to three missionary journeys across the Roman Empire. Authored 13 epistles (Romans through Philemon) that form the theological backbone of the New Testament, establishing doctrines of grace, justification by faith, and the universal Church.
